[decision] arch.scylla-standard-to-xcloud-no-inplace — NO in-place Standard->X Cloud conversion (type is creation-time; tablets vs vNode = migrate-to-new-cluster). LOW impact for us: Scylla data tiny (E2E+R2 offload) + app env-only (swap SCYLLA_KNOWN_NODES). Trade: Standard-then-migrate (cheaper Alpha, 1 small migration) vs X-Cloud-day-1 (no migration ever, +$1.35k/mo Alpha) (status: verified)
[decision] arch.scylla-ondemand-vs-scaling-model — Standard vs X Cloud: 'On Demand' = hourly billing cadence (BOTH); REAL difference = SCALING MODEL — Standard=fixed-size-you-manage ($1.662/hr flat), X Cloud=auto-size-policy ($3.512/hr initial, varies, +forced Vector Search). Standard for steady Alpha, X Cloud for growing Beta (status: verified)

CORRECTED reco: Standard for small Alpha, X Cloud for variable Beta. ($1,071/mo annual-upfront vs $1,213/mo on-demand = same cluster, diff billing) (status: verified)

[decision] arch.security.scylla-public-endpoint-protection-layers — Public-Scylla protection = 5-layer defense-in-depth: IP-allowlist(stable via connector) + TLS + SASL + E2E-AEAD(#1431, DB holds ciphertext not plaintext) + media-token-only. Breach yields encrypted blobs. Alpha=public+layers; Beta=VPC-peering layer-0 (status: verified)
[decision] arch.scylla-no-vpc-required-public-allowlist — NO VPC REQUIRED: CF container (enableInternet=true) does native raw-TCP :9142 egress to Scylla PUBLIC endpoint + TLS + IP-allowlist (both docs confirm). VPC peering = OPTIONAL hardening. Tunnel = optional (stable IP only). Real blocker = locked Sandbox cluster, never VPC (status: verified)
[decision] arch.scylla-address-translator-3node-tunnel — 3-node tunnel translator: probe BUILT but laptop allowlist-blocked (Connect timeout) — can't discover from here. DNS resolves the 3 hostnames to PUBLIC IPs (100.x/18.x matching console). FIX: runtime self-discovering AddressTranslator (matches+logs each discovered peer -> loopback port) — sidesteps chicken-and-egg + public-vs-internal uncertainty (status: verified)
[decision] ops.scylla-tunnel-contact-point-count — Scylla TUNNEL = single-node via 127.0.0.1:9142 loopback (NOT the 3 public cloud hostnames). Driver 1.6 reads rpc_address=public scylla.cloud hostnames from system.peers -> would dial discovered nodes OUTSIDE the tunnel. Functional single-node-routed for TEST; PROD VPC-peering reaches all 3 directly (status: done)
[decision] ops.chat-service-cloudflared-tunnel-scylla-steps — Scylla tunnel route = PUBLISHED APPLICATION (public hostname -> tcp://scylla:9142), gated by CF Access self-hosted app + Service Token. NOT Private hostname (that needs WARP/Gateway/Cf-One-Client). cloudflared access tcp sidecar in chat-service container dials 127.0.0.1:9142 (status: done)
[decision] arch.security.scylla-network-isolation-two-phase — Scylla isolation 2-phase + PUBLIC-vs-PRIVATE attack-surface rationale: TEST=public+tunnel+Access-token (acceptable, test cluster); PROD-at-scale=VPC Peering (NO public endpoint -> attackers cannot reach the DB at all). Private removes the IP-allowlist as the weakest layer. cloudflared connector bridges both (status: done)
